pr_comments:
Should `UV_NO_BUILD` work for `uv pip install` commands as well?
I have a Linux host, where `gcc` is not available for certain reasons. Running below command still wants to invoke gcc upon installing:
`UV_NO_BUILD=1 uv pip install caio`

Whereas `uv pip install caio --no-build` works.
No, I don't believe those are respected in the `uv pip` CLI since the interface is a little different to match `pip`. E.g., in `uv pip`, you need to do `--no-build :all:`.
We want to thread these through to there, I think — we just haven't done it yet.

Oh, it also says right in the commit message, my bad. 🙂
> for non-pip commands.

issue_context.title: `UV_NO_BUILD` and `UV_NO_BUILD_PACKAGE` environment variables
issue_context.body:
### Summary

Environment variables to allow specifying packages to only use the wheels of instead of building from source.

### Example

The following:

```
UV_NO_BUILD_PACKAGE='cryptography rpds-py' uv sync --no-binary
```

Would be equivalent to:

```
uv sync --no-binary --no-build-package cryptography --no-build-package rpds-py
```
comments: Yep, very similar. The use cases I'm looking for are with `sync` and not with `uv pip`, but they're essentially the expansion of https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/11399 for the `no-build` variants.

If you call those relationships out ahead of time you'll save me time :)

Sounds good though, these make sense to add.
Sorry about that! I'll try to remember for the future.

review_comments: A bit of an aside, but this is pretty surprising! cc @charliermarsh
